description: Driven by innovation, we are a multidisciplinary team for NASA Space Apps. Led by Zainab (AppsClub VP, data analytics and web development), our crew includes Rida (storytelling & pitch), Afaf & Othmane (game/interactive design and coding), and Houda & Issam (cybersecurity & backend). We fuse spatial data analytics, secure architecture, and user-centered design into impactful open-source solutions.
summary: We developed an educational survival game for children aged 7–12 that turns screen time into real learning about space. Built on real NASA data, the game puts players in charge of a space colony where they must manage finite resources such as oxygen and energy, choose which buildings to run, and respond to incoming warnings about environmental events. Every decision has consequences, but over a 10-day cycle new options appear that let players conserve resources and reduce damage, teaching them to balance consumption with regeneration and plan ahead. This matters because many children’s games blur the line between fiction and reality without offering accurate information, and a study published in Psychology of Popular Media found that children were more likely to mistake fantasy images for reality after just 15 minutes of gameplay. Our game replaces that confusion with science-based experiences, helping children understand what survival on another planet really requires.
details: Our game places children aged 7–12 in charge of a space colony built on real NASA data. Players manage the colony’s buildings and resources by deciding which structures consume supplies such as oxygen and energy, balancing consumption with regeneration because resources are finite. Over a 10-day cycle, they receive warnings about upcoming phenomena and must choose how to respond; every choice has consequences, but later options let them conserve resources and reduce the damage. This teaches planning, trade-offs, and how a planet’s environment changes over time, through play rather than memorization. Our intended impact is to turn gaming into a chance to understand what survival really requires, helping children tell what is real from what is fictional and sparking an early interest in space science.
